title: Declined, Invoiced and Paid work orders only reorder within their technician
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  4. Look at the {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3} and {Work-order-4} cards and hover the lock or any marker on them.
  5. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card above {Work-order-1}'s card inside {Technician-A}'s column and release it.
  6. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column and release it.
  7. Drag {Work-order-3}'s card into the Unassigned column and release it.
  8. Drag {Work-order-6}'s card from Unassigned into {Technician-A}'s column and release it.
  9. Drag {Work-order-4}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column and release it, then drag {Work-order-5}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column and release it.
  10. Click Tech View in the display switcher.
  11. Drag {Work-order-3}'s row into {Technician-B}'s group and release it.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3} each show a lock icon, which marks that they can only be reordered within {Technician-A}'s work, not moved to another technician. Hovering the lock shows "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" on {Work-order-2} and "Paid · can’t be reassigned" on {Work-order-3}. {Work-order-4} (Declined) also shows a lock icon, and hovering it shows "Declined · can’t be reassigned".
  • Step 5: {Work-order-2} moves above {Work-order-1}. Reordering within the same technician is allowed.
  • Steps 6 and 7: {Work-order-2} cannot be dropped on {Technician-B} and {Work-order-3} cannot be dropped on Unassigned. While {Work-order-2} is over {Technician-B}'s column, the note "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" shows at the top of that column. Both stay in {Technician-A}'s column, no lead-change message appears and {Technician-A}'s count is unchanged.
  • Step 8: {Work-order-6} cannot be moved out of Unassigned. It stays there.
  • Step 9: {Work-order-4} (Declined) cannot be dropped on {Technician-B}: while its card is over {Technician-B}'s column the note “Declined · can’t be reassigned” shows at the top of that column, and it stays in {Technician-A}'s column. {Work-order-5} (Complete) moves to {Technician-B}'s column, with the message "{Work-order-5} assigned to {Technician-B}", with an "Undo" button.
  • Step 11: the same rule holds in Tech View. While {Work-order-3}'s row is over {Technician-B}'s group, the note "Paid · can’t be reassigned" shows at the top of that group, and {Work-order-3} stays in {Technician-A}'s group.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns); SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S9-N1, S4-N2, S4-N7, S4-N6 and S4-R5, read 19 Oct 2026. In version 48 (12 Oct 2026) S4-N2 dropped Imported from the locked statuses (Imported work orders now open in List only); the Invoiced and Paid rules this case checks are unchanged, so the expected results are unchanged. In version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward ruling on the design-difference sheet) S4-N6 gave the lock icon and the drag note the design's words, and S4-R5 made the message after a move "{work order number} assigned to {technician name}", with Undo; the results of steps 4, 6, 9 and 11 follow. Review Decisions page 853901313, DR-37 (25 Sep 2026), whose "Declined moves freely" was replaced in PRD version 82 (29 Oct 2026, SV-11902). Tech plan (revised 24 Sep 2026) section 3.23. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Known problem (SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the message after a lead change reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

PRD version 82 (29 Oct 2026, SV-11902; read 29 Oct 2026): a Declined work order now locks its lead technician exactly like an Invoiced or Paid one (S4-N2, S4-N6, S4-N7, S4-R32); Complete work orders still move freely. The results of steps 4 and 9 follow, and the quotes below are from version 82. The Declined behaviour was seen on the QA branch sv11902 (build v26.43.3-74314c9) on 29 Oct 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-N1: “Apply S4-N1 and S4-N2’s permission and status restrictions to every work order drag.”
  • S4-N2: “Do not allow the lead technician to change in Declined, Invoiced or Paid status. A Declined, Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today. The lock follows the work order’s status at the moment of the change: a work order is Declined only while every one of its lines is declined, so when a line is re-approved or a new line is added and the work order becomes Estimate or Approved, its lead can change again. Only the work order’s own status counts: a declined line on a work order in any other status does not lock it.”
  • S4-N7: “Visually indicate that a Declined, Invoiced or Paid work order can only be reordered within its current technician, not moved to another one.”
  • S4-N6: “On a Declined, Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Declined · can’t be reassigned”, “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, in the design’s format. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • Tech plan 3.23 lead lock vs reorder: “In a locked status a work order can be dragged within its current technician (or within Unassigned if it has no lead); it cannot be dropped on another technician, and cannot move between a technician and Unassigned.”
